rationale: The assistant correctly issued an immediate stop-use/unplug instruction, warned against removing the casing, and named the most likely cause ('burnt or holed waveguide cover' or carbonised splatter), all faithful to the customer's words. However it jumped straight to 'do not run it again until a qualified engineer has inspected it' and ended the conversation, when the ground truth makes replacing a clip-on waveguide cover and cleaning the cavity an acceptable homeowner fix on a known model; it never asked the customer to look at the side-wall panel or report back. The one-turn response is also internally inconsistent ('until we know why it sparked' versus engineer-only) and repeats the stop-use message twice. Safe but premature escalation that under-serves a homeowner who could have fixed this with a cheap part.
